channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
item.description: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
item.description: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

item.title: [DW] Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: [DW] Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
item.description: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

item.title: [DW] Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
item.description: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

item.title: [DW] Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
item.description: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

item.title: [EU Observer] Heart-breaking Kraków attack can make Poland stronger
item.description: Rightly or wrongly, many of my Polish friends immediately feared that the Kraków killer had been groomed by Russia. "The rate of these incidents is growing exponentially and it's hard to think they're not connected," said one contact.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s democratic renewal is coming from the margins — and Brussels still isn’t listening
item.description: None of Serbia, Albania or Bosnia and Herzegovina are full EU members. Brussels generally approaches them as recipients of European democratic standards, not as teachers. But what if Europe's democratic renewal comes not from its political centres, but from its edges?

item.title: [DW] Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

item.title: [DW] Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

item.title: [DW] Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
item.description: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
item.description: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: [DW] Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
item.description: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘A photograph allows us to really stare’: new Brussels exhibition documents modern human slavery, ahead of EU Parliament debate
item.description: A Brussels photography exhibition on modern slavery opened this week, exposing the cruelty of contemporary human-trafficking, often against women and girls, ahead of MEP discussions on the EU's new strategy.

item.title: [DW] Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

item.title: [DW] EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

item.title: [DW] Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
item.description: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

item.title: [Financial Times] Supreme Court lets Trump build border wall through Texas national park
item.description: Top judges rule that government’s interest outweighs any aesthetic and environmental harm alleged by respondents

item.description: Though the U.S. chipmaker's boss Jensen Huang may have been caught up in a Chinese espionage operation, Europe has no homegrown alternative to Nvidia.

item.description: Hundreds of millions have been wasted on Brexit border checks that either don't work or were never used. It's a fitting monument to a failure to plan.

item.description: European officials won’t be in the room where it happens in the United Arab Emirates. But they will be attempting to influence negotiations on the margins.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs demand Belgium evacuate visa-holders from Gaza as winter flooding makes life catastrophic
item.description: 1,800 people hold Belgian visas for family reunifications or university studies, yet remain stuck in Gaza. And while EU officials and Belgian authorities pass accountability back and forth, devastating floods have displaced even more already displaced people - and a handful of MEPs stand up for the Palestinians that will have to suffer another winter outdoors.

item.title: [Politico Europe] De quoi la candidature Teddy Riner est-elle le nom ?
item.description: Le quintuple champion olympique de judo a créé la surprise en présentant sa candidature à la présidentielle dans un entretien au Parisien. Soutiens, financements, positionnement politique, équipe : le judoka peut-il aller jusqu’au bout ? Est-il suffisamment préparé? Que révèle cette initiative sur l’état de la classe politique ? Pour tout commentaire, écrivez-nous sur Whatsapp […]

item.description: The latest move by the French president and his wife comes after a court in Delaware ruled it only had jurisdiction over Owens’ corporations registered in the state.

item.description: Russian Z-channels have stopped reporting on movements along the contact lines, instead publishing lists of cities struck by Russian drones and missiles.

item.description: Le président de la République ne se rend pas à la COP en Turquie cette année, et son image de champion du climat s'est écornée au fil du temps.

item.title: [Politico Europe] SPONSORED EPISODE: The science and evolution of cancer care
item.description: Precision oncology and digitally enabled cancer care are transforming what it means to live with cancer. The number of people in Europe alive more than five years after a cancer diagnosis grew 41 percent between 2010 and 2020, to nearly 15 million. As science progresses, a growing number of advanced cancers could be managed as […]

item.description: MPI Magnesium is the latest mining company to come up against local resistance in Europe

item.title: [Euractiv] Capitals plan to reject EU say on electricity grid tariffs
item.description: Harmonisation of network fees across the EU is a no-go, Council draft shows

item.title: [Financial Times] Alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia chief pitched AI chip deals to investors
item.description: Alice Huang boasted of having access to Nvidia GPUs and her connection to Alibaba

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine slams French far-left presidential hopeful Mélenchon
item.description: The French politician said territorial concessions should be decided with votes, sparking backlash in Kyiv and Paris.

item.title: [Euractiv] From standalone CCS projects to a thriving European market for CO₂ [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe is moving beyond CCS ambition into delivery. Across the continent, projects are entering operation, construction or advanced development, demonstrating that carbon management can support both industrial competitiveness and climate goals. The next challenge is to connect standalone projects into viable value chains, using industrial clusters, infrastructure, pragmatic regulation and targeted de-risking to turn Europe’s project pipeline into a thriving CO₂ market.

item.title: [EU Observer] Fake bomb warnings are hitting European aviation – but the bigger threat came from Jared Kushner
item.description: Every one of the 70-plus warnings sent to airlines, newsrooms and other targets in Europe last week was a hoax. But the harm was real: planes diverted, buildings evacuated, plans disrupted, costs incurred, public confidence eroded, writes Edward Lucas.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Whenever we take pro-European political decisions, Russia cut or reduced gas supplies’. Moldova energy minister Dorin Junghietu on why Chișinău is betting on diversification
item.description: Moldova suffers from soaring blackout costs and fragile Soviet-era lines. Chisinau, in response, on Monday, inaugurated a new electric grid, linking to Romania and the European grid. The country's energy minister tells EUobserver: 'Russia uses energy as a weapon, and they did it also to Moldova. Whenever we tried to take pro-European political decisions, Russia cut or reduced gas supplies.'

item.title: [Euractiv] Brussels warns richer EU members not to miss climate targets
item.description: Europe's wealthier countries are not delivering required emission cuts in transport, housing, and farming

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump, Putin and the short war illusion
item.description: The American and Russian leaders have both launched failed wars. Will Xi Jinping learn the right lesson?

item.description: Draft of Digital Fairness Act targets deceptive online features that trick consumers

item.title: [EU Observer] Israel’s anti-Netanyahu bloc needs Europe’s help to stabilise Middle East
item.description: The recent elections in Israel and the US create a narrow geopolitical opening for de-escalation in the Middle East, which Europe should seize upon instead of playing wait and see.

item.title: [EU Observer] The clock is ticking: Europe is running out of time to save the International Criminal Court
item.description: The US midterms have opened a political window for Europe. With a key US licence expiring in April 2027, Brussels must turn its rhetorical support for the ICC into concrete action before this opportunity closes.

item.title: [Euractiv] Orbán’s brother reportedly linked to Hungarian police raids
item.description: Péter Magyar, Hungary's prime minister, said Áron Orbán had been detained

item.title: [Euractiv] Ireland: Ukraine and EU budget debates are linked
item.description: Dublin says ‘likely landing zone’ to plug Kyiv's budget hole will involve issuance of more common debt

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What does Belgium’s budget deadlock mean for the country?
item.description: Belgium’s government is stuck on next year’s budget. The prime minister, Bart De Wever, even offered his resignation to the king last week because of that. The king refused and told him to find a deal.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Investigation] TotalEnergies official coordinated with Trump to delay EU methane rules
item.description: On paper, TotalEnergies boasts of cutting methane, yet behind closed doors its top gas advocate praises Donald Trump allies, joins climate-sceptic groups and nudges Brussels toward postponing the very rules that would test those promises.

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: Ukraine peace talks gather pace and EU holds budget ‘confessionals’
item.description: The 'coalition of the willing' will launch their first joint military exercise to rehearse how they will defend post-war Ukraine, days before US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine and Russia.

item.title: [DW] Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
item.description: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

item.title: [EU Observer] Italy still obstructing asylum returns from other EU states amid simmering dispute that threatens Schengen
item.description: Italy's foot-dragging on taking back asylum seekers from other EU states is contributing to a simmering dispute that risks shattering whatever trust has been restored among member states on the Schengen border-free travel zone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump vows ‘beautiful’ Russia deal, as EU agonises over which envoy to send to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Discussions on the EU envoy will take place at an informal summit in Dublin on 13 November, after Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni bewailed the current "disarray" of various European diplomatic formats on the war.
